issues.failure_explanation: The formal characterization is an if-and-only-if result for tubal-length optimality. The only stated bridge proves that tubal-length optimality implies multirank and t-rank optimality. That direction gives sufficiency, not necessity, for the existing rank notions. No converse or direct necessity argument for t-rank or multirank optimality is supplied, so the advertised complete characterization of products yielding those Eckart-Young results does not follow.

failure_location.quote: In this paper, we provide a complete characterization of the family of tubal products that yield an Eckart-Young type result.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must prove the missing converse or give direct necessity proofs for t-rank and multirank optimality, or else restrict all characterization claims to tubal-length optimality and present the rank results as sufficient conditions only.
issues.overall_effect: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion materially overstate the scope of the formal characterization, particularly its claimed necessity for t-rank and multirank truncations.
issues.title: Advertised necessity for t-rank and multirank is not established
issues.why_classification: Without a new necessity argument, the paper must withdraw a central advertised guarantee and replace a complete characterization by a one-sided sufficient condition.

issues.failure_explanation: The existence, for each singular generator, of some generating-set element having a nonzero pairing does not make those indices distinct, so it does not imply $r'\ge r$. Over a product-of-fields ring, generators supported on orthogonal idempotent components can be combined into one generator and recovered by multiplying by the corresponding idempotents. The later nonfreeness argument has the same defect: every displayed coefficient contains $\bs{t}_j\mm\bs{p}_j=0$, so the alleged linear combination is trivial, not nontrivial.

failure_location.quote: Showing that for all $j \in [r]$ there exists $k \in [r']$ such that $\bs{s}_{j,j} \mm \vec{\matW}_k^\CT \mm  \tU_{:,j} \neq \bs{0}$, hence $r' \geq r$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the generator-count argument with a correct componentwise module analysis and weaken or remove the minimality and nonfreeness claims; generators supported on different simple components must be allowed to combine.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted geometric interpretation of t-rank as the minimum number of generators is false, and the subsequent blanket argument that a proper support idempotent makes the whole image module nonfree is unreliable.
issues.title: Nonzero singular tubes need not form a minimal module generating set
issues.why_classification: The false module-theoretic claims require more than a local algebra correction, but the later tubal-length construction can potentially proceed using the canonical component decomposition without preserving these claims.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting the displayed mixed-term identity into the preceding formula gives a plus sign on the $2\Re(g_{s',s})$ term and a minus sign on the $4\Im(g_{s',s})$ term. Equation `eq:nec.intra.Frob.norm.tA.tB.final` reverses both signs. The two subsequent counterexamples and their error comparisons are computed from that erroneous formula, so they do not establish that the real and imaginary parts of $g_{s',s}$ vanish.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must recompute the weighted Frobenius norm correctly and construct valid counterexamples, or supply a replacement necessity argument proving both parts of $g_{s',s}=0$.
issues.overall_effect: The necessity of orthogonality within conjugate row pairs is unproved, and hence the necessity direction of the paper's central characterization theorem is unreliable.
issues.title: Intra-component necessity counterexamples use an incorrect norm expansion
issues.why_classification: The failed calculation supports a central necessity direction, and the source contains no valid replacement argument showing that a comparable characterization survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The globally selected threshold $\nu_{r_\gamma}$ can exceed every singular value in a particular frontal slice. Then the set whose maximum defines $\rho_i$ is empty, and no convention assigning rank zero is provided. The range of the maximization index is also unspecified.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define $\rho_i=0$ when no singular value in slice $i$ reaches the threshold, and explicitly restrict $\rho$ to the available diagonal indices; a tie policy should also be specified.
issues.overall_effect: The algorithm and the universally quantified quantity $r_\gamma(\matM)$ are not well-defined on all stated inputs.
issues.title: Adaptive truncation algorithm is undefined for empty slice selections
issues.why_classification: A standard local convention makes the procedure executable without changing its basic method, although it does not repair the independent false comparison theorem.

issues.failure_explanation: Nonuniform row scaling can concentrate transformed-domain energy and thereby reduce, rather than increase, the number of sorted entries needed to reach a threshold. For example, in a two-component real product ring with scalar transformed slices of equal unscaled squared energy, $\matM_0=I$, $\matM_1=\operatorname{diag}(100,1)$, and $\gamma=0.9$, the unscaled execution needs both entries while the scaled execution needs only the first. Thus $r_\gamma(\matM_0)=2>1=r_\gamma(\matM_1)$. The proof's equality between $1-\beta_r$, an energy fraction measured after the nonunitary transform, and an original-domain relative Frobenius error is invalid for nonuniform $\matD$.
